function.name: powershell
function.description: Run a PowerShell command in the current working directory (via {exe}). PREFER THIS OVER bash ON WINDOWS: bash falls through to cmd.exe here, which has no sleep, no grep, no sed, and breaks on input redirection. Native exit codes are preserved exactly; a failing cmdlet reports 1. Returns stdout and stderr, truncated to the last 2000 lines or 50KB. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds (default 120). Pass background=true to fire and forget a long command; its result comes back later as a message.

background.description: true = do not wait: returns at once with a task id while the command keeps running. Its output arrives later as a message tagged [inbox from task], and the full output is at output/tasks/<id>.log (read it with the read tool). Set timeout to the long budget you want, e.g. 3600. Use for anything that takes minutes.
